alignment.route: seis2018 pdfPage 92-93, printedPage 2-40 to 2-41: from the new underground station beneath Townsend Street, three tracks continue east under Townsend Street, curve north at about Clarence Place just east of Third Street, run under Second Street for approximately 0.4 mile, and enter the train box beneath the Transit Center, which extends to the east side of Beale Street. Construction by cut-and-cover and mined tunneling (ftaProfileAR26 p.1).
alignment.tracksInTunnel: 3 tracks between Fourth and Townsend Street Station and Salesforce Transit Center (seis2018 printedPage 2-41; phasingStudy2021 p.7)

stations.name: Fourth and Townsend Street Station (new, underground)
stations.description: Realigned in the 2018 SEIS to lie 'along and underneath Townsend Street' at Fourth Street, lowered with a mezzanine added, beneath the Muni Metro T-Line on Fourth Street; station facilities (entrances, vents) within the Townsend Street right-of-way (seis2018 pdfPage 110, printedPage 2-58; pdfPage 247, printedPage 2-195). Previously approved (No Action) station was 'beneath Townsend Street between Fourth and Fifth Streets' (seis2018 printedPage 2-40).
stations.platforms: Two tracks with one center platform and two side platforms (tjpaWebAbout)
stations.hsrStop: No. The 'Fourth and Townsend CHSRA Platform Elimination' secondary mitigation ($101m reduction) was adopted in the 2025 cost update (tjpaBoard2025_07_item11 slide 4, pdfPage 13); HSR would stop only at the Transit Center.
stations.connections: Direct transfer to Muni Central Subway / T-Third (phasingStudy2021 p.48 of 83, section 6.4.3)

geocode.method: geocode: OSM node 65334473, the 4th Street / Townsend Street intersection (traffic_signals). Not a published station centroid; the station box runs along Townsend Street from about this corner (exact extent not published in the documents read).

stations.name: Salesforce Transit Center (train box fit-out)
stations.description: Existing two-level train box beneath the Transit Center, about 60 ft below ground, 1,500 ft long by about 190 ft wide, built 2010 with up to $400 million ARRA funds, extending easterly to the east side of Beale Street; tracks narrow from six to three at the west end just east of Second Street (seis2018 pdfPage 98, printedPage 2-46). Six tracks with three center platforms (tjpaWebAbout).
stations.address: 425 Mission Street, San Francisco 94105 (OSM addr tags); SFCTA describes the location as 'First and Mission Streets' (sfctaCacMemo2026_01 p.6)

service.ftaServiceDescription: Service planned 4:30 am to 1:30 am weekdays and 6:00 am to 1:30 am weekends, trains every 10 to 15 minutes in weekday peak periods and every 30 minutes off-peak and weekends (ftaProfileAR26 p.1).

longRange.seis2018: Blended system envisions up to 10 trains per peak hour per direction to and from San Francisco: six Caltrain and four HSR tpph/d; how many proceed to the Transit Center to be determined later (seis2018 pdfPage 99, printedPage 2-47).
longRange.phasingStudy2021: Integrated peak service in 2040 of eight Caltrain and four high-speed trains per hour per direction on the DTX (8+4); 3 tunnel tracks support 12 tph/direction (phasingStudy2021 p.7; section 4, page 11 of 83).
longRange.sfctaScope2026: Traction power simulation for a 2035 scenario of 6 (8-car) Caltrain trains and 4 (8-car) CHSRA trains (sfctaCacMemo2026_01, GEC scope, pdf text line ~1526)

travelTime.scheduledRunTime_note: No published Caltrain or TJPA run time for the 4th & Townsend to Transit Center tunnel segment was found. The SEIS gives only the non-revenue move between the railyard and the below-grade Fourth and Townsend station: 'approximately 10 minutes' including the turnback (seis2018 pdfPage 120, printedPage 2-68). A model should compute run time from the 1.3 mi distance.

savingsClaims.source: feis2004ch3 pdfPage 33-34, printedPage 3-33 to 3-34, Table 3.1-16 (Parsons Ridership Model, September 2001)

reduce commute times into downtown San Francisco by up to 30 minutes and avoid the current need to transfer from Caltrain to a bus or light rail

travelTime.interpretation: The per-trip saving with model-based support is 13-15 min (2004 FEIS) or 15-30 min (2008 Cambridge, Mountain View example) for downtown-bound riders versus a 4th & King + Muni/walk connection; the 30-45 min and 'almost an hour' figures are per-day (two-way) promotional statements without a cited model run.

ftaCig2023Submittal.source: ftaProfileAR26 p.1 Summary Description (identical in ftaProfileEng2024 p.1 and ftaProfileFY25 p.1)
ftaCig2023Submittal.model: FTA STOPS (tjpaBoard2023_08_item9 pdfPage 49: 'Long-term (~2045) forecast consistent with FTA "STOPS" model and FTA May 2023 Guidance considering both pre- and post-pandemic ridership'); prepared by SFCTA with Caltrain and TJPA under FTA guidance
ftaCig2023Submittal.currentYearDefinition: Per FTA May 2023 guidance as summarized by the sponsors: two forecasts, 'pre-covid' baselined from 2019 and 'post-covid' baselined from 2022 or 2023; FTA rates the project using 'Base year to equal post-Covid, plus a defined bump-up' and 'Horizon year (2045) to be average of pre and post' (escMemo2023_07 slide 9, pdfPage 15; memo p.4). The 2023 figure is therefore a current-year (no land-use growth) forecast on modified post-COVID conditions, not observed ridership.
ftaCig2023Submittal.assumptions: 4 Caltrain trains pphpd to Transit Center, PCEP electrification complete, Caltrain sole rail operator (no HSR) (tjpaBoard2023_08_item9 pdfPage 8, 49). MTC consultant notes the 2023 STOPS analysis 'uses pre-pandemic data and is underpinned by PBA2040 forecasts (as opposed to the more recent PBA2050)' (mtcStageGate2025 slide 12).
ftaCig2023Submittal.interpretation: 'Daily linked trips' on an FTA profile are trips that use the project (here, rider trips using the Portal segment/its two stations), counted once per linked trip; they are neither Caltrain systemwide ridership nor new riders. This is the number most comparable to a model run on today's population and jobs.
ftaCig2023Submittal.notPublished: The profiles do not publish the mobility/cost-effectiveness/congestion/environmental measures (trips on the project by transit-dependent persons, new/auto-diverted trips, travel-time savings hours). Only Land Use (High) and Economic Development (Medium-High) detail pages (rating assigned May 2023) are printed (ftaProfileAR26 p.6).

ridership.stationBoardings2023Forecast_note: No station-level boardings (Transit Center vs 4th & Townsend) from the 2023 STOPS/CIG forecasts were found in any published TJPA, SFCTA, Caltrain, MTC, or FTA document. SFCTA says it 'will lead ridership forecasting efforts, at such time as FTA requires these forecasts to be updated in support of seeking the FFGA' (sfctaCacMemo2026_01 p.2).

currentYearEstimate.unit: daily linked trips on the project
currentYearEstimate.caveat: FTA current-year scenario = today's population/jobs and network with the project added, using a modified post-COVID 2023 base 'plus a defined bump-up' (escMemo2023_07 slide 9). It is a weekday-type daily figure from STOPS; the profile states 5,130,400 annual linked trips (ratio 310.9). No other published no-growth estimate was found.

cost.summary: $8.255 billion YOE (FTA Engineering entry, incl. $375.4M finance charges and $728.5M already-built train box); indicative update $7.57 billion (July 2025); FTA CIG maximum $3,384,462,235 (41%).
cost.sources: ftaProfileAR26 p.1; tjpaBoard2025_07_item11 pdfPage 1-2 and slide 3; sfctaBoard2026_02 slide 5 (total $7,572M; $8.25B approved August 2023; both include $729M train box).
